resources.name: Illinois Lawyers' Assistance Program (LAP)
resources.confidential: Guaranteed; Illinois Supreme Court Rule 1.6(d) mandates confidentiality for LAP
resources.description: Statewide 501(c)(3) for Illinois judges, lawyers, and law students (and families): assessments, counseling, peer support, interventions, group meetings, and treatment referrals for substance use, stress, anxiety, burnout, and depression.

resources.name: Indiana Judges and Lawyers Assistance Program (JLAP)
resources.confidential: Confidential under Admission & Discipline Rule 31 §9 and RPC 8.3(c)
resources.description: Indiana Supreme Court program (Admission & Discipline Rule 31) for judges, lawyers, and law students: intake support, follow-up consultations (in person/phone/video), volunteer peer pairing, and several recurring support groups.

resources.name: Iowa Lawyers Assistance Program (ILAP)
resources.confidential: Free and confidential; no identifying information disclosed; no reporting relationship
resources.description: Private nonprofit helping Iowa judges, attorneys, and law students obtain treatment for substance use, addiction, and mental-health issues, with monitoring. Verified via an archived snapshot of iowalap.org (live site has a TLS cert mismatch).

resources.name: Esquire Assistance Program (EAP)
resources.operator: Iowa Judicial Branch, Office of Professional Regulation (third-party EAP vendor)

phones.label: 1-800-EAP-IOWA
phones.hoursNote: 24/7/365 confirmed verbatim on the official (archived) page

resources.confidential: Confidential; not shared with the OPR, employer, or judiciary except as required by law
resources.cost: Free (up to 3 in-person/telehealth sessions per concern + 24/7 phone counseling)
resources.description: License benefit for all Iowa-licensed lawyers, judges, and court reporters (and families): three free counseling/telehealth sessions plus 24/7 phone access, via a third-party EAP vendor. Verified via an archived snapshot of the official iowacourts.gov page.

resources.name: Kansas Lawyers Assistance Program (KALAP)
resources.operator: Kansas Supreme Court / Kansas Judicial Branch
resources.confidential: Confidential by Kansas Supreme Court Rule 233
resources.description: Statewide program of the Kansas Supreme Court (Rule 233): confidential counseling, support groups, mentoring, interventions, and referrals for lawyers, judges, and law students. A companion Judges Assistance Committee serves judges via the same office.

resources.name: KALAP 24/7 EAP Providers Helpline
resources.operator: KALAP outsourced Employee Assistance Program provider

phones.label: Confidential EAP helpline (after-hours)
phones.hoursNote: Page: 'KALAP has a 24/7 helpline staffed with trained mental health professionals'

resources.description: After-hours confidential helpline staffed by an outsourced EAP provider, giving Kansas lawyers 24/7 support when KALAP staff are out of office.

resources.name: Kentucky Lawyer Assistance Program (KYLAP)
resources.operator: Kentucky Bar Association (KY Supreme Court Rules 3.900-3.995)

phones.label: KYLAP direct line (24/7; after hours routes to EAP)
phones.hoursNote: Page: 'Contact us 24 hours a day at (502) 226-9373'

resources.description: Statewide confidential program for lawyers, judges, and law students: assessment/treatment referrals, peer support, recovery meetings, monitoring, and financial assistance for substance use and mental-health impairment.

resources.name: Kentucky Bar Association Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
resources.operator: Kentucky Bar Association / KYLAP partner EAP vendor

phones.label: KYLAP direct line — after hours connects to EAP
phones.hoursNote: Page: 'Someone will be available to you 24 hours a day, 7 days a week'

resources.cost: Free (up to 4 clinical sessions, no income test)
resources.description: KBA/KYLAP-partnered EAP giving lawyers and judges up to four free clinical sessions and referral to a statewide provider network (appointment in 24-48 hours), reachable 24/7 via the KYLAP direct line.

resources.name: KYLAP Foundation
resources.confidential: Part of the confidential KYLAP program
resources.cost: Forgivable loans for mental-health/addiction treatment (incl. medications)
resources.description: 501(c)(3) providing financial assistance to lawyers for mental-health treatment (incl. medications and addiction treatment) as forgivable loans; may also make loans for disciplinary/bar-dues costs. Verified on kylap.org/get-involved/ (the /foundation URL 404s).

resources.name: Judges and Lawyers Assistance Program (JLAP)
resources.operator: Judges and Lawyers Assistance Program, Inc. (owned/funded by the Louisiana State Bar Association)
resources.confidential: Privileged and confidential by law (La. R.S. 37:221); not subject to subpoena
resources.cost: Free (call/consult/assessment); $50/mo only for a formal monitoring contract, deferrable/waivable for hardship
resources.description: Full-service statewide program (501(c)(3) owned by the LSBA, operating independently) for lawyers, judges, law students, and families: assessment, referral, intervention, monitoring, support groups, and family support.

resources.name: Maine Assistance Program for Lawyers and Judges (MAP)
resources.operator: Maine Assistance Program for Lawyers and Judges, Inc.
resources.confidential: Confidential under Maine Rev. Stat. Title 14 §164-A(3)
resources.description: Independent 501(c)(3) (est. 2002 by rule of Maine's Supreme Judicial Court): confidential peer assistance, referral, and support groups for the bench, bar, law students, and applicants.

resources.name: Maryland Lawyer Assistance Program (LAP)
resources.description: MSBA program for Maryland lawyers, judges, law students, and support staff: virtual/in-person assessment, referral, short-term counseling, peer support, and financial assistance for mental-health and addiction treatment.

resources.name: Lawyers Concerned for Lawyers, Inc. (LCL)
resources.description: Private nonprofit (est. 1978), Massachusetts' sole LAP: free confidential consultations, clinical mental-health services, addiction-recovery and peer-support groups, practice-management help, and peer monitoring for lawyers, judges, law students, and families.

resources.name: Lawyers and Judges Assistance Program (LJAP)
resources.description: State Bar of Michigan program for attorneys, law students, bar applicants, judges, and families: clinical assessments, short-term counseling, provider referrals, monitoring, training, and free confidential virtual support groups.

resources.name: Lawyers Concerned for Lawyers (LCL)

phones.label: LCL main line
phones.hoursNote: Business hours; 24/7 crisis via partner AllOne Health

resources.description: Minnesota's statewide LAP (est. 1976, partly Supreme Court-funded): clinical assessments and referrals, interventions, short-term counseling, licensed-counselor support groups, and peer mentoring for lawyers, judges, law students, and families.

resources.name: AllOne Health (LCL counseling partner)

phones.label: 24-hour counseling line
phones.hoursNote: Page: 'available by phone 24 hours a day, seven days a week'

resources.confidential: Confidential; nothing revealed to LCL without written permission (except imminent-danger exceptions)
resources.cost: Up to 4 free sessions through LCL
resources.description: LCL's outsourced clinical/EAP counseling partner: confidential face-to-face and 24/7 phone counseling with addiction-specialized clinicians; first four sessions free through LCL.

resources.name: Mississippi Lawyers and Judges Assistance Program (LJAP)

phones.label: Office (toll-free)
phones.hoursNote: Labeled 'Office (toll-free)' on the official page — no 24-hour claim

resources.confidential: All communication held in the strictest confidence; not affiliated with any disciplinary authority
resources.cost: Confidential assistance (no fee stated on the official page)
resources.description: Program authorized by the Mississippi Supreme Court: intervention, referral for evaluation/treatment, monitoring, and limited treatment for judges, lawyers, law students, staff, and families. Verified via an archived snapshot of the official msbar.org page, which labels the toll-free line an office line (not a 24-hour hotline).
